marta: Seeing a new tail-latency pattern on prod GPUs after yesterday's kernel selector change — lots of 95/99 spikes on long-context chat sessions. spike started ~02:10 UTC, correlated with eviction activity.

siva: Any quick numbers?

marta: p90 ~ 40ms (unchanged), p95 jumped from 75ms -> 210ms, p99 up to ~480ms on some nodes. Token throughput same.

noah: That's pretty big. Did the KV pager logs show increased page-ins or more reinsert churn?

marta: Pager shows a burst of evict+reinsert cycles — small entries being evicted then immediately read back during long contexts. The pattern looks like repeated FIFO wins on hot entries.

jen: Wait — yesterday's change biased kernel selection to prefer the new fused attention kernel for medium sequence lengths. Could that change request batching characteristics and make small KV entries get reaccessed more often?

siva: Possibly. Batching heuristics shift request coalescing window; if many requests are now served in slightly different time slices, KV access locality could be disrupted, exposing eviction ordering issues.

marta: I pulled a short perf profile (perf-bot attached) — flame graph shows hot path in kv.reinsert_and_touch() with long tails. Also saw lock contention on the bucket-level mutex.

perf-bot: Attached: /s3/perf/4081239876/kv-reinsert-flame.svg (small), /s3/perf/4081239876/pager-stats.log

noah: Can you paste the pager summary?

marta: paste: ```pager: evict_rate=480/s reinsert_rate=320/s page_in_rate=122/s hot_hit=0.61 cold_miss=0.39 avg_entry_size=512 bytes fragmentation_ratio=0.27```

jen: hot_hit dropping <0.7 is suspicious for long contexts. Also fragmentation_ratio 0.27 could amplify memory walking cost.

siva: Could be an LRU vs FIFO tie — when under bursty pressure, our FIFO implementation reinserts at tail causing recently-used small entries to be moved out. If the kernel change produces lots of tiny-interval repeats, FIFO could thrash. LRU would keep them but we had reasons to try FIFO for simpler offload.

marta: Repro on staging: ran a 30-minute long-context replay (seq_len ~6k tokens) with the new kernel selector; saw identical spikes. Rolling back kernel selector to previous config removed spikes.

noah: Great repro. Suggestion: add a short probation window on evicted entries — if an entry is re-inserted within X ms, treat it as 'resurrect' and promote it to head, or temporarily pin small entries under high reinsert rates. Cheap heuristics reduce churn.

jen: Agreed. Another quick mitigation: widen batching coalesce window by 2ms to reestablish access locality. Might be lower-risk than changing eviction logic mid-release.

siva: Both sound reasonable. For correctness: confirm our eviction invariants still hold under concurrent reinsert+evict racing (we had a bug there earlier where reinserts could create duplicate handles). Can someone run the stress correctness harness with concurrent eviction enabled?

marta: Starting stress run now with race-detector + new counters (dup_handle_count). Will post results in ~20m.

perf-bot: FYI /metrics shows a small uptick in kv.lock_wait_ms correlating with the spikes.

noah: If duplication counter >0 we have correctness bug. If zero but thrash persists, it's a policy mismatch.

jen: If we implement probation, keep it bounded (e.g., 5s or 50 reaccesses) and gated behind a runtime flag. We'll canary on a small fleet.

marta: Stress run update: dup_handle_count=0, but reinsert_rate remains high under the test load and p95 still elevated. So no correctness duplication — it's policy/pressure.

siva: Ok. Plan: 1) revert kernel selector for rolling rollback to relieve immediate pain (jen to coordinate), 2) implement temporary probation/promotion logic behind a flag + unit tests (noah), 3) experiment with batching coalesce window (marta). Canary target: next 6 hours.

jen: I'll start rollback PR and schedule canary. Add telemetry: track reinsert_latency histogram and resurrect_count metric.

noah: I'll prototype probation logic tonight and add a microbenchmark. Keep the policy simple: if reinsert within 250ms or <=3 reaccesses, promote. We'll log when resurrects exceed threshold.

marta: Thanks. Also adding a tracepoint in pager to record evict order and timestamps so we can prove the root cause.

perf-bot: Noted. Follow-up: please tag this thread when the canary is live. :thumbsup:

siva: Thanks team — good triage. We'll reconvene after canary results or if anything spikes further.
